reconcile.connective: Historic commentators read the repeated "first and last" formula as Christ knowingly claiming Jehovah's own self-description, not borrowing a rival title.

discrepancy.connective: The sharpest objection comes from Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible, which catalogs this exact pairing as a direct contradiction, not a Trinity proof-text.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (skepticsannotatedbible.com, est. 1999; print ed., SAB Books, 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: the first . . . the last-- (Isa 41:4; Isa 44:6; Isa 48:12). From eternity, and enduring to eternity: "the First by creation, the Last by retribution: the First, because before Me there was no God formed; the Last, because after Me there shall be no other: the First, because from Me are all things; the Last, because to Me all things return" [RICHARD OF ST. VICTOR].
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Cross-references the exact Isaiah triad (41:4; 44:6; 48:12) to Revelation 1:17 and glosses the shared title as Christ's own eternality ("before Me... after Me"), i.e. the harmonizing move that identifies Christ with YHWH rather than treating the two claims as unrelated.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), notes at Isaiah 48:12 and Revelation 1:17
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill's notes on both verses read Isaiah's 'I am he, I am the first, and I also am the last' and Christ's identical words in Revelation as one and the same self-designation, offered explicitly as proof of Christ's true and proper deity rather than as two rival claimants to the title. (Haley's Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible, 1874, was checked and does not treat this specific pairing; Gill is used as the surfaced harmonizing commentator per the fallback rule.)

link.title: GotQuestions: What is the Trinity?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment stating that Isaiah 48's divine self-descriptions, including 'the first and the last,' are applied directly to Jesus in Revelation 1:17 and 22:13 as Trinitarian evidence.
